newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha spreads broader amid tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha spreads broader amid tight supplies.

text.p: Naphtha spreads became steeper in afternoon Tokyo trade on Monday as regional availability for prompt cargoes remained tight, traders said.
"End-users found it quite difficult to procure near-term cargoes such as first-half January," one trader said.
The inter-month naphtha spread between second-half January and second-half February was assessed at plus $5.00/7.00, compared with plus $3.50/5.00 in late last week.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half February was quoted at $227.00/228.00. It was traded at $229.00 on Friday.
Bids for second-half January were heard at $230.00, while offers were notionally assessed at $232.00.
Tight availability was partly attributed to a delay in the startup of a new crude distillation unit in South Korea and a scheduled turnaround at Saudi Arabia's Jubail refinery.
In physical naphtha trading, one petrochemical firm located in Chiba said it bought one spot cargo for first-half January delivery. The price was not available.
Levels for first-half January cargoes were assessed by traders at around $9.00 over the mean of Japanese quotes.
